{{Distinguish|text=the [[K-distribution]] of probability distributions}}
{{notability|date=February 2023}}
In [[statistics]], a '''Kaniadakis distribution''' (also known as '''κ-distribution''') is a statistical distribution that emerges from the [[Kaniadakis statistics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2021-01-01 |title=New power-law tailed distributions emerging in κ-statistics (a) |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |journal=Europhysics Letters |volume=133 |issue=1 |article-number=10002 |doi=10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |arxiv=2203.01743 |bibcode=2021EL....13310002K |s2cid=234144356 |issn=0295-5075}}</ref> There are several families of Kaniadakis distributions related to different constraints used in the maximization of the [[Kaniadakis statistics#Kaniadakis_entropy|Kaniadakis entropy]], such as the [[Kaniadakis Exponential distribution|κ-Exponential distribution]], [[Kaniadakis Gaussian distribution|κ-Gaussian distribution]], [[Kaniadakis Gamma distribution|Kaniadakis κ-Gamma distribution]] and [[Kaniadakis Weibull distribution|κ-Weibull distribution]]. The κ-distributions have been applied for modeling a vast phenomenology of experimental statistical distributions in natural or artificial [[complex system]]s, such as, in [[epidemiology]],<ref>{{Cite The κ-distributions are written as function of the κ-deformed exponential, taking the form

:<math> f_i=\exp_{\kappa}(-\beta E_i+\beta \mu) </math>

enables the power-law description of complex systems following the consistent [[Kaniadakis statistics|κ-generalized statistical theory]].,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=Giorgio |date=2013-09-25 |title=Theoretical Foundations and Mathematical Formalism of the Power-Law Tailed Statistical Distributions |journal=Entropy |language=en |volume=15 |issue=12 |pages=3983–4010 |doi=10.3390/e15103983 |arxiv=1309.6536 |bibcode=2013Entrp..15.3983K |issn=1099-4300|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2001 |title=Non-linear kinetics underlying generalized statistics |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |language=en |volume=296 |issue=3–4 |pages=405–425 |doi=10.1016/S0378-4371(01)00184-4|arxiv=cond-mat/0103467 |bibcode=2001PhyA..296..405K |s2cid=44275064 }}</ref> where <math> \exp_{\kappa}(x)=(\sqrt{1+ \kappa^2 x^2}+\kappa x)^{1/\kappa} </math> is the Kaniadakis κ-exponential function.

The κ-distribution becomes the common Boltzmann distribution at low energies, while it has a power-law tail at high energies, the feature of high interest of many researchers.

== List of κ-statistical distributions ==

=== Supported on the whole real line ===
[[File:Kaniadakis Gaussian Distribution Type II pdf.png|thumb|337x337px|Plot of the κ-Gaussian distribution for typical κ-values. The case κ=0 corresponds to the normal distribution.]]
* The [[Kaniadakis Gaussian distribution]], also called the κ-Gaussian distribution. The [[normal distribution]] is a particular case when <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0.</math>
* The Kaniadakis double exponential distribution, as known as Kaniadakis κ-double exponential distribution or κ-Laplace distribution. The [[Laplace distribution]] is a particular case when <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0.</math><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=da Silva |first1=Sérgio Luiz E. F. |last2=dos Santos Lima |first2=Gustavo Z. |last3=Volpe |first3=Ernani V. |last4=de Araújo |first4=João M. |last5=Corso |first5=Gilberto |date=2021 |title=Robust approaches for inverse problems based on Tsallis and Kaniadakis generalised statistics |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1140/epjp/s13360-021-01521-w |journal=The European Physical Journal Plus |language=en |volume=136 |issue=5 |page=518 |doi=10.1140/epjp/s13360-021-01521-w |bibcode=2021EPJP..136..518D |s2cid=236575441 |issn=2190-5444|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Supported on semi-infinite intervals, usually [0,∞) ===
[[File:Kaniadakis Gamma Distribution pdf.png|thumb|340x340px|Plot of the κ-Gamma distribution for typical κ-values.]]
* The [[Kaniadakis Exponential distribution]], also called the κ-Exponential distribution. The [[exponential distribution]] is a particular case when <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0.</math>
* The [[Kaniadakis Gamma distribution]], also called the κ-Gamma distribution, which is a four-parameter (<math>\kappa, \alpha, \beta, \nu</math>) deformation of the [[Generalized gamma distribution|generalized Gamma distribution]].  
** The [[Kaniadakis Gamma distribution|κ-Gamma distribution]] becomes a ...
*** [[Kaniadakis Exponential distribution|κ-Exponential distribution]] of Type I when <math>\alpha = \nu = 1</math>.
*** κ-Erlang distribution when <math>\alpha = 1</math> and <math>\nu = n = </math> positive integer.
*** [[Kaniadakis Half-Normal distribution|''κ''-Half-Normal distribution]], when <math>\alpha = 2</math> and <math>\nu = 1/2 </math>.
*** [[Generalized gamma distribution|Generalized Gamma distribution]], when <math>\alpha = 1</math>;
** In the limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>, the [[Kaniadakis Gamma distribution|κ-Gamma distribution]] becomes a ...
*** [[Erlang distribution]], when <math>\alpha = 1</math> and <math>\nu = n = </math> positive integer;
*** [[Chi-squared distribution|Chi-Squared distribution]], when <math>\alpha = 1</math> and <math>\nu =  </math> half integer;
*** [[Nakagami distribution]], when <math>\alpha = 2</math> and <math>\nu > 0 </math>;
*** [[Rayleigh distribution]], when <math>\alpha = 2</math> and <math>\nu = 1 </math>;
*** [[Chi distribution]], when <math>\alpha = 2</math> and <math>\nu = </math> half integer;
*** Maxwell distribution, when <math>\alpha = 2</math> and <math>\nu = 3/2 </math>;
*** [[Half-normal distribution|Half-Normal distribution]], when <math>\alpha = 2</math> and <math>\nu = 1/2 </math>;
*** [[Weibull distribution]], when <math>\alpha > 0</math> and <math>\nu = 1 </math>;
*** [[Stretched Exponential distribution]], when <math>\alpha > 0</math> and <math>\nu = 1/\alpha </math>;

=== κ-Distribution Type IV ===
{{Short description|Continuous probability distribution}}
{{Infobox probability distribution
  | name       = ''κ''-Distribution Type IV
  | type       = density
  | parameters = <math> 0 \leq \kappa < 1 </math> <br /> <math> \alpha > 0</math> [[shape parameter|shape]] ([[Real number|real]]) <br /> <math> \beta> 0 </math> [[rate parameter|rate]] ([[Real number|real]])
  | support    = <math>x \in [0, +\infty)</math>
  | pdf        = <math>  \frac{\alpha}{\kappa} (2\kappa \beta )^{1/\kappa } \left(1 - \frac{\kappa \beta x^\alpha}{\sqrt{1+\kappa^2\beta^2x^{2\alpha} } } \right) x^{ -1 + \alpha / \kappa} \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha) </math>
  | cdf        = <math> (2\kappa \beta )^{1/\kappa} x^{\alpha / \kappa} \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha)</math>
  |moments=<math> \frac{(2 \kappa \beta)^{-m/\alpha} }{ 1 + \kappa \frac{ m }{ 2\alpha } }  \frac{\Gamma\Big(\frac{1}{\kappa} + \frac{m}{\alpha}\Big) \Gamma\Big(1 - \frac{m}{2\alpha}\Big)}{\Gamma\Big(\frac{1}{\kappa} + \frac{m}{2\alpha}\Big)} </math>|pdf_image=FILE:Kaniadakis typeIV Distribution pdf.png|pdf_caption=Plot of the κ-Distribution Type IV for typical κ-values, and <math> \alpha = \beta = 1 </math>.|cdf_image=FILE:Kaniadakis typeIV Distribution cdf.png}}
The '''Kaniadakis distribution of Type IV''' (or '''κ-Distribution Type IV''') is a three-parameter family of [[Probability distribution|continuous statistical distributions]].<ref name=":0" />

The κ-Distribution Type IV distribution has the following [[probability density function]]:

: <math> 
f_{_{\kappa}}(x) = \frac{\alpha}{\kappa} (2\kappa \beta )^{1/\kappa} \left(1 - \frac{\kappa \beta x^\alpha}{\sqrt{1+\kappa^2\beta^2x^{2\alpha} } } \right) x^{ -1 + \alpha / \kappa} \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha)
</math>

valid for <math>x \geq 0</math>, where <math>0 \leq |\kappa| < 1</math> is the entropic index associated with the [[Kaniadakis statistics#Kaniadakis_entropy|Kaniadakis entropy]], <math>\beta > 0</math> is the scale parameter, and <math>\alpha > 0</math> is the shape parameter.

The [[Cumulative distribution function|cumulative distribution]] function of κ-Distribution Type IV assumes the form:

: <math>F_\kappa(x) = (2\kappa \beta )^{1/\kappa} x^{\alpha / \kappa} \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha) </math>

The κ-Distribution Type IV does not admit a classical version, since the probability function and its cumulative reduces to zero in the classical limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

Its [[Moment (statistics)|moment]] of order <math>m</math> given by

: <math>\operatorname{E}[X^m] = \frac{(2 \kappa \beta)^{-m/\alpha} }{ 1 + \kappa \frac{ m }{ 2\alpha } }  \frac{\Gamma\Big(\frac{1}{\kappa} + \frac{m}{\alpha}\Big) \Gamma\Big(1 - \frac{m}{2\alpha}\Big)}{\Gamma\Big(\frac{1}{\kappa} + \frac{m}{2\alpha}\Big)}</math>

The moment of order <math>m</math> of the κ-Distribution Type IV is finite for <math>m < 2\alpha</math>.
